files.history.moved.defaultMessage: The branch has moved since this list was read.
files.history.moved.description: HI-3475: a bar atop the History panel: the folder's checked-out commit changed (a commit, a switch) since the list was read; Refresh reads it again.

files.history.noMerge.defaultMessage: No merge brought it in that Combwork can name
files.history.noMerge.description: HI-3475: a History row, after Find its merge: the commit was made on the branch itself, or how it came in isn't clear (several branches merged at once), so nothing is said.

files.history.none.defaultMessage: No commit has changed this yet.
files.history.none.description: HI-3475: the History panel for a file or folder no commit has changed (new, or not tracked by git).

files.history.notFile.defaultMessage: {side, select, left {Before this commit: a folder or submodule, not a file} other {After this commit: a folder or submodule, not a file}}
files.history.notFile.description: HI-3475: above a commit's diff from History when one side is a folder or a submodule at that path. Keep the select keys.

files.history.notThere.defaultMessage: {side, select, left {Before this commit: not in that version} other {After this commit: not in that version}}
files.history.notThere.description: HI-3475: above a commit's diff from History when one side has no file: the commit added the file (left) or deleted it (right). Keep the select keys.

files.history.openCard.description: HI-3475: the tooltip of a commit's card in the History panel. {card} is its key (HI-12), {title} its title.

files.history.openCommit.description: HI-3475: a History row's button: opens the Commit dialog (the commit's message, files and actions).

files.history.pick.defaultMessage: Select one file or folder to see its history.
files.history.pick.description: HI-3475: the History panel when nothing, or several items, are selected in the Files tab.

files.history.refresh.description: HI-3475: the History panel's button: reads the history again from the folder's current commit.

files.history.renamed.description: HI-3475: in a History row: this commit renamed the file; {path} is the path it had before.

files.history.retry.description: HI-3475: the History panel's button after reading failed.

files.history.submittedBy.description: HI-3475: in a History row, after the card: the agent ({agent}, its name) that submitted this commit for review in one of the card's submissions. Not who wrote it.

files.history.submittedByTip.defaultMessage: {agent} submitted this commit for review in one of {card}'s submissions. It doesn't say who wrote it: git records one author for everyone here.
files.history.submittedByTip.description: HI-3475: the tooltip of 'submitted by' in a History row. {agent} is the agent's name, {card} the card's key.

files.history.title.description: HI-3475: the heading of the Files tab's History panel: the commits that changed the file or folder selected.

files.history.toggle.description: HI-3475: the Files tab's toolbar button (and right-click menu item) that shows or hides the History panel: the commits that changed the file or folder.

files.history.toggleTip.defaultMessage: The commits that changed this, with their cards
files.history.toggleTip.description: HI-3475: the tooltip of the Files tab's History button.

files.image.actualSize.description: Tooltip on an image fitted to the pane.

files.image.fit.description: Tooltip on an image shown at its actual size.

files.insertIntoSession.description: Button or menu item: attaches the file to the agent's running session.

files.links.title.description: The hover of a file path in a terminal (an agent's output): Ctrl+click opens the file in the project's Files tab. Files is the tab's name: use it as the tab is named.

files.loading.description: Shown while the attachments (or one of them) load.

files.menu.copy.description: Files tab's right-click menu: copies the files (to paste elsewhere).

files.menu.copyPath.description: Menu item or button: copies the full path to the clipboard.

files.menu.copyRelativePath.description: Files tab's right-click menu: copies the path within the project.

files.menu.duplicate.description: Files tab's right-click menu: copies the files beside themselves.

files.menu.insertPath.description: Files tab's right-click menu and toolbar: attaches the files to the agent's running session.

files.menu.newFile.description: Files tab's right-click menu and toolbar: creates a file.

files.menu.newFolder.description: Files tab's right-click menu and toolbar: creates a folder.

files.menu.openInDefaultApp.description: Files tab's right-click menu and toolbar: opens the file in its Windows app.

files.open.description: Button: opens a file in its default Windows app.

files.openFailed.description: Title of an error notification: a file could not be opened (read, or opened in its default app).

files.refresh.description: Button or menu item: reads the folder (or the attachments) again.

files.restore.becomes.description: HI-3477: above the right side of the confirmation's diff: the file as it will be, from that commit ({commit}, a short id).

files.restore.binary.description: HI-3477: in place of the confirmation's diff when the file is binary.

files.restore.discard.description: HI-3477: the Files tab's right-click menu, for a changed file: puts it back to the commit checked out, after showing what it would undo. Its changes go to a stash.

files.restore.discardButton.description: HI-3477: the button of the confirmation before Discard Changes.

files.restore.discardMessage.defaultMessage: It goes back to the commit checked out ({commit}). Its changes are kept in a stash: Apply in Version Control → Changes → Stashes brings them back.
files.restore.discardMessage.description: HI-3477: the confirmation before Discard Changes. {commit} is a short commit id.

files.restore.discardTitle.description: HI-3477: title of the confirmation before Discard Changes. {name} is the file.

files.restore.discarded.description: HI-3477: notification after Discard Changes. {name} is the file.

files.restore.discarding.description: HI-3477: Discard Changes' button while it runs.

files.restore.failed.description: Title of an error notification after the Files tab's Discard Changes… or Restore From… (HI-3477).

files.restore.from.description: HI-3477: the Files tab's right-click menu, for a file git tracks: opens a menu of where to take the file's version from (the target branch, a commit).

files.restore.fromCommit.description: HI-3477: a choice under Restore From: opens a list of the commits that changed the file, to pick one.

files.restore.fromTarget.description: HI-3477: a choice under Restore From: the file's version on the project's target branch ({target}, its name).

files.restore.missingInCommit.defaultMessage: The file isn't in {commit} (that commit deleted it): pick another.
files.restore.missingInCommit.description: HI-3477: under the commit list of Restore From → A Commit…, when the commit picked ({commit}, a short id) has no file at this path.

files.restore.missingMessage.defaultMessage: The target ({commit}) has no file at this path: there is nothing to restore it from.
files.restore.missingMessage.description: HI-3477: the note Restore From → Target Branch shows when the file is not on the target. {commit} is a short commit id.

files.restore.missingTitle.description: HI-3477: title of the note Restore From → Target Branch shows when the file is not on the target branch ({target}, its name). {name} is the file.

files.restore.noCommits.defaultMessage: No commit on this branch changed this file.
files.restore.noCommits.description: HI-3477: in Restore From → A Commit… when the file has no commits on the branch checked out.

files.restore.now.description: HI-3477: above the left side of the confirmation's diff: the file as it is now, what Discard or Restore replaces.

files.restore.pickFirst.description: HI-3477: an error in Restore From → A Commit… when Restore is pressed before a commit is picked.

files.restore.readFailed.description: HI-3477: in Restore From → A Commit… when reading the commits or a diff failed. {error} is why.

files.restore.restoreButton.description: HI-3477: the button of the confirmation before Restore From.

files.restore.restoreMessage.defaultMessage: {source, select, target {It becomes its version on {target} ({commit}),} other {It becomes its version in the commit you pick,}} as a change to commit. {changed, select, yes {Its uncommitted changes are kept in a stash first (Version Control → Changes → Stashes).} other {It has no uncommitted changes: nothing is lost.}}
files.restore.restoreMessage.description: HI-3477: the confirmation before Restore From. target: from the target branch ({target}, its name; {commit} a short commit id); other: from a commit the user picks in the list below. {changed}: yes when the file has uncommitted changes, which are stashed.

files.restore.restoreTitle.defaultMessage: {source, select, target {Restore "{name}" from {target}?} other {Restore "{name}" from a commit}}
files.restore.restoreTitle.description: HI-3477: title of the confirmation before Restore From. {name} is the file; target: from the target branch ({target}, its name); other: from a commit the user picks.

files.restore.restored.description: HI-3477: notification after Restore From. {name} is the file; {commit} a short commit id.

files.restore.restoring.description: HI-3477: Restore From's button while it runs.

files.restore.same.defaultMessage: No difference: the file on disk is already this version.
files.restore.same.description: HI-3477: in place of the confirmation's diff when the file on disk is the same as the version it would become.

files.restore.stashedNote.defaultMessage: Its earlier changes are in Version Control → Changes → Stashes.
files.restore.stashedNote.description: HI-3477: under the notification after Discard Changes or Restore From, when the file had changes, which were stashed.

files.reveal.description: Short button: shows the file in Windows File Explorer.

files.revealInExplorer.description: Button or menu item: shows the file or folder in Windows File Explorer.

files.root.place.description: The Files tab's folder picker: the folder an agent works in. {agent} is the agent's name, {place} where (agents.place.short: "in slot-b", "carried: hb2", "home: hr4").

files.root.projectFolder.description: The Files tab's folder picker: the project's own folder.

files.root.tip.defaultMessage: Show the project folder, or the folder an agent works in: its slot or worktree
files.root.tip.description: Tooltip on the Files tab's folder picker, shown when agents work outside the project folder (in slots, Combwork's worktrees lent to cards, or their own worktrees from before 1.0).

files.root.worktree.description: The Files tab's folder picker: a worktree agent's folder. {agent} is the agent's name, {branch} its git branch.

files.save.description: Button in a file editor's toolbar: saves the file.

files.saveAll.changedOnDisk.defaultMessage: {file}: changed on disk since you opened it
files.saveAll.changedOnDisk.description: Why Save All did not save a file: it changed on disk meanwhile. {file} is its path in the project.

files.trash.button.description: Button: moves the files or attachments to the Recycle Bin.

files.trash.detail.defaultMessage: You can restore it from the Recycle Bin.{unsaved, plural, =0 {} =1 { Unsaved changes to {file} will be lost.} other { Unsaved changes to # files will be lost.}}
files.trash.detail.description: Under the confirmation before deleting in the Files tab. {unsaved} is how many of the files have unsaved edits; {file} the one such file.

files.trash.message.defaultMessage: Move {count, plural, =1 {{folder, select, yes {"{name}" and everything in it} other {"{name}"}}} other {# items}} to the Recycle Bin?
files.trash.message.description: The confirmation before deleting in the Files tab. {name} is the one file or folder ({folder} is yes for a folder); {count} how many are selected.

files.trash.title.description: Title of the confirmation before files or attachments go to the Recycle Bin.

files.tree.empty.description: The Files tab's list for a project folder with nothing in it.

files.unsavedChanges.description: Tooltip on the dot beside a file that has unsaved edits.

files.view.binary.description: Shown in place of a file Combwork cannot show as text.

files.view.changedBanner.defaultMessage: {name} has changed on disk since you opened it.
files.view.changedBanner.description: Banner over an open file with unsaved edits that changed on disk. Followed by Reload and Overwrite with Mine. {name} is the file name.

files.view.changedBody.defaultMessage: Reload it, or overwrite it with your version.

files.view.changedTitle.description: Title of a warning when saving a file that changed on disk since it was opened. {name} is the file name.

files.view.discardMessage.defaultMessage: Reload {name} from disk and discard your unsaved changes?
files.view.discardMessage.description: Confirmation before reloading a file. {name} is the file name.

files.view.discardTitle.description: Title of the confirmation before reloading a file with unsaved edits from disk.

files.view.edit.description: A file view's mode button: the text editor.

files.view.gone.defaultMessage: This file no longer exists on disk. Save to recreate it.
files.view.gone.description: Banner over an open file that was deleted on disk.

files.view.htmlPreview.description: Accessible title of the frame that shows an HTML file's preview.

files.view.image.description: A file view's mode button: an image file (or SVG) shown as a picture.

files.view.notUtf8.defaultMessage: This file isn't UTF-8 text, so Combwork can't edit it without changing its characters.
files.view.notUtf8.description: Shown in place of a text file in another encoding (such as Windows-1252), which the editor would corrupt on save. UTF-8 is the encoding's name: keep it as it is.

files.view.openInApp.defaultMessage: Open it in its default app instead.
files.view.openInApp.description: Under "This is a binary file." or "This file is too large to open here", above an Open button.

files.view.overwrite.description: Button in the "changed on disk" banner: saves your version over the file on disk.

files.view.pdf.description: A file view's mode button: a PDF shown in the PDF viewer.

files.view.pdfPreview.description: Accessible title of the frame that shows a PDF file.

files.view.preview.description: A file view's mode button: the rendered Markdown or HTML.

files.view.reload.description: Button: reads the file from disk again, dropping unsaved edits.

files.view.saveFailed.description: Title of an error notification. {name} is the file name.

files.view.saveTip.description: Tooltip on the Save button. Keep Ctrl+S as it is.

files.view.split.description: A file view's mode button: the editor and the preview side by side.

files.view.table.description: A file view's mode button: a CSV or TSV file shown as a table.

files.view.tooLarge.defaultMessage: This file is too large to open here ({size}).
files.view.tooLarge.description: Shown in place of a file too large for the editor. {size} is its size, such as "12.4 MB".

files.viewer.newer.description: Tooltip on the attachment viewer's left arrow. Keep the arrow.

files.viewer.noPreview.defaultMessage: No preview for this kind of file. Show it in its folder, or insert it into a session.
files.viewer.noPreview.description: The attachment viewer for a file it cannot show. Show in Folder and Insert into Session are its buttons (the second only while an agent runs).

files.viewer.older.description: Tooltip on the attachment viewer's right arrow. Keep the arrow.

files.viewer.openInApp.description: A button in the attachment viewer (HI-1958), for an image or a PDF only: opens it in the program Windows opens that kind of file with (its photo viewer, its PDF reader), for zooming, printing and the like. Other kinds of file are never opened (nothing attached is ever run): they get Show in Folder instead.

files.viewer.position.description: The attachment viewer's footer: which attachment of how many is shown.

files.viewer.readFailed.description: The attachment viewer when the file can't be read. {error} is why (from Windows, may be English).

files.viewer.removeFromCard.description: A button in the attachment viewer for a card's attachment (HI-1958): takes the file off its card (to the Recycle Bin), after asking. A session's attachment has Delete there instead.

files.viewer.tooLarge.defaultMessage: Too large to preview here. Reveal it to open it in another program.
files.viewer.tooLarge.description: The attachment viewer for a file too large to show.
